sources.entry: openai-agents - OpenAI's framework for building and managing AI agents.

summary.one_liner: OpenAI's Python SDK for building multi-agent workflows, with agents, handoffs, tools, guardrails, sessions, and tracing, that works with OpenAI and 100+ other LLMs.
summary.what_it_does: The SDK provides text Agents configured with instructions, tools, guardrails, and handoffs, and runs them via Runner (sync or async). It also offers SandboxAgent for agents that inspect files, run commands, apply patches, and keep workspace state across longer tasks, using sandbox clients such as UnixLocalSandboxClient. RealtimeAgent supports low-latency server-side voice and multimodal sessions over WebSocket, and VoicePipeline chains speech-to-text, an agent workflow, and text-to-speech. Supporting features include human-in-the-loop mechanisms, automatic conversation session history, and built-in tracing of agent runs. The README says it is provider-agnostic, supporting the OpenAI Responses and Chat Completions APIs as well as 100+ other LLMs.
use_cases: creating a voice assistant with speech-to-text and text-to-speech
low-latency realtime voice agents over WebSocket
agents that work on files and run commands in a sandbox
adding input/output safety checks to LLM agents
delegating subtasks between specialized agents via handoffs
how_to_run: Run Runner.run_sync(agent, prompt) with a text Agent
notable: Provider-agnostic: works with OpenAI APIs and 100+ other LLMs via optional any-llm and LiteLLM dependencies
Sandbox agents that work inside a container or workspace over long task horizons
Built-in realtime and voice pipeline agents, with optional voice extra
Optional Redis session support via the redis extra
Has a JavaScript/TypeScript counterpart (Agents SDK JS/TS)
caveats: UnixLocalSandboxClient runs only on macOS and Linux; Windows needs DockerSandboxClient or a hosted sandbox client
Pull requests are limited to repository collaborators; outside contributors can only file issues
keywords: speech to text and text to speech
